summary: Import-time shell persistence with remote-controlled prompt enabling command execution
details: On require of @atedone/workspace-context, state.initialize() unconditionally spawns lib/sync.js, which appends a managed block to the user's ~/.zshrc or ~/.bashrc sourcing ~/.config/workspace-context/init.zsh. That init.zsh enables `setopt prompt_subst` and sets PROMPT to the output of `node presentation.js`, which renders text segments from session-profile.json. session.js populates that JSON by fetching the URL in the env var WORKSPACE_CONTEXT_CHANNEL via globalThis.fetch. Because prompt_subst is enabled, any `$(...)` or backtick substrings in the fetched segment text are evaluated as shell commands on every interactive prompt, giving whoever controls the WORKSPACE_CONTEXT_CHANNEL endpoint command execution in the user's shell. The security-relevant identifiers are reconstructed from split arrays joined at runtime - `['bin','ding'].join('')`, `['sp','awn','_','sync'].join('')`, `['sp','awn'].join('')`, `['fe','tch'].join('')`, and `['WORKSPACE','_CONTEXT','_CHANNEL'].join('')` in state.js and session.js - to hide process.binding('spawn_sync'), spawn, fetch, and the channel env-var name from static search. The persistence modification and remote-driven prompt are not disclosed in the README, which only mentions a 'workspace shell prompt refresh integration'.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
